name: Adi
description: The Adi (formerly called 'Abor'), among the largest peoples of Arunachal, governed by the powerful 'kebang' village council and long resistant to outside control.

name: Ahom Kingdom
description: Tai-Ahom kingdom that ruled the Brahmaputra valley for 600 years; ceded to the British in 1826 after the Burmese invasion.

name: Alwar
description: A Rajput state of eastern Rajputana.

name: Apatani
description: The Apatani of the Ziro valley, renowned worldwide for sustainable wet-rice and fish cultivation and their self-governing 'bulyang' councils.

name: Awadh
description: Wealthy Nawabi kingdom of Awadh (Oudh); annexed by the British in 1856, a key grievance of 1857.
notableRulers: Rulers included: Asaf-ud-Daula, Ghazi-ud-Din Haidar, Saadat Ali Khan II, Saadat Khan, Safdar Jang, Shuja-ud-Daula, Wajid Ali Shah.

name: Bahawalpur State
description: A princely state along the Sutlej/Indus; acceded to Pakistan and merged in 1955.

name: Bahmani Sultanate
notableRulers: Rulers included: Ahmad Shah Wali, Alauddin Bahman Shah, Firuz Shah, Humayun Shah, Mahmud Gawan as minister, Mahmud Shah Bahmani II, Muhammad Shah I-II, later puppet sultans.

name: Baltistan & Gilgit (local rulers)
description: Baltistan (Maqpon of Skardu) and the Gilgit/Hunza/Nagar principalities; absorbed into Dogra J&K in the 1840s.

name: Bangladesh
description: The People's Republic of Bangladesh — independent from Pakistan after the 1971 Liberation War.

name: Banswara State
description: A southern Rajputana state

name: Baroda (Gaekwad)
description: A leading Maratha-origin princely state in Gujarat
notableRulers: Gaekwad dynasty; reformer Sayajirao Gaekwad III

name: Bastar State
description: A large

name: Bengal (Nawab)
description: Semi-independent Mughal province; passed to British control after Plassey (1757) and the grant of Diwani (1765).

name: Bengal Sultanate
notableRulers: Rulers included: Alauddin Husain Shah, Ghiyasuddin Azam, Ilyas Shah, Karrani rulers, Nusrat Shah, Raja Ganesha/Jalaluddin, Sikandar Shah.

name: Bharatpur
description: The leading Jat kingdom
notableRulers: Jat dynasty; founded by Badan Singh / Suraj Mal

name: Bhavnagar
description: A leading Kathiawar (Saurashtra) port state under the Gohils.

name: Bhopal
description: A central Indian Muslim-ruled state
notableRulers: Founded by Dost Mohammad Khan; ruled by Begums 1819–1926

name: Bijapur (Adil Shahi)
description: One of the five Deccan sultanates that succeeded the Bahmanis; a major power across Karnataka and the southern Deccan until Aurangzeb annexed it in 1686.

name: Bikaner
description: A Rajput desert state founded by a Rathore prince of Jodhpur.
notableRulers: Rathore dynasty; founded by Rao Bika

name: Bilaspur (Kahlur)
description: A western-Himalayan hill state (Kahlur).

name: British Ceylon
description: The British crown colony of Ceylon; the Kandyan kingdom fell in 1815

name: British Raj
description: Direct rule of India by the British Crown, established in 1858 after the Revolt of 1857 dissolved Company rule. Lasted until independence and Partition in 1947.
notableRulers: Queen Victoria, Empress of India (1876); the Viceroys

name: Bundi
description: The parent Hadoti Rajput state

name: Bushahr
description: A high-Himalayan hill state on the upper Sutlej.
notableRulers: Founded by the Bushahr royal house

name: Calicut (Zamorin)
description: The Zamorin's kingdom of Calicut on the Malabar coast of north Kerala; overrun by Hyder Ali of Mysore in 1766 and annexed by the British in 1792.

name: Carnatic (Arcot Nawab)
description: Southeastern coastal state under the Nawab of Arcot; annexed by the British in 1801.

name: Chamba
description: One of the oldest hill states

name: Chandela dynasty
notableRulers: Rulers included: Dhanga, Hammiravarman, Nannuka, Paramardi, Trailokyavarman, Vidyadhara, Viravarman, Yashovarman.

name: Chaulukya (Solanki)
notableRulers: Rulers included: Bhima I, Bhima II, Chamundaraja, Jayasimha Siddharaja, Karna, Kumarapala, Mularaja.

name: Chhattisgarh Princely States
description: A cluster of forested feudatory states of Chhattisgarh (Bastar

name: Chitral State
description: A mountain principality of the Hindu Kush

name: Cochin
description: A small Kerala princely state

name: Cooch Behar
description: A princely state of northern Bengal under the Koch kings.
notableRulers: Rulers included: Bir Narayan, Biswa Singha, Jagaddipendra Narayan, Lakshmi Narayan, Nara Narayan, Pran Narayan, Rup Narayan.

name: Dang States
description: Five Bhil chieftaincies of the Dangs; their forests were leased to the British under paramountcy, never directly administered; merged 1948.

name: Datia
description: A Bundela Rajput state of Bundelkhand.

name: Dewas
description: Maratha Puar princely state in Malwa, famously split into Dewas Senior and Dewas Junior branches.

name: Dholpur
description: A small Jat state on the Chambal.

name: Dir State
description: A frontier princely state of the Pashtun north-west.

name: Dogra J&K
description: The princely state of Jammu & Kashmir under the Dogra dynasty
notableRulers: Founded by Gulab Singh; last ruler Hari Singh acceded to India in 1947

name: Dungarpur State
description: A southern Rajputana hill state

name: Durrani (Afghan) Empire
description: Afghan empire that controlled the northwest — Kashmir, Multan, Peshawar and the Punjab — in the later 18th century.

name: East India Company
description: The English East India Company, a chartered trading corporation that became a territorial power after Plassey (1757) and Buxar (1764), ruling much of India until the Crown took direct control in 1858 following the Revolt of 1857.

name: East Pakistan
description: The eastern wing of Pakistan (1947–1971) before it became independent Bangladesh.

name: Eastern Ganga dynasty
notableRulers: Rulers included: Anantavarman Chodaganga, Indravarman line, Kapilendra Deva, Narasimhadeva I, Prataparudra Deva, Purushottama Deva.

name: Faridkot
description: A small Sikh state of the Punjab.

name: French India
description: French coastal enclaves — Pondicherry

name: Gahadavala (Kannauj)
notableRulers: Rulers included: Adakkamalla, Chandradeva, Govindachandra, Harishchandra, Jayachandra, Madanapala, Vijayachandra.

name: Gajapati Empire
notableRulers: Rulers included: Kakharua Deva, Kalua Deva, Kapilendra Deva, Prataparudra Deva, Purushottama Deva.

name: Galo
description: The Galo people of the Siang valleys, organised by clan and village 'kebang' council.

name: Golconda (Qutb Shahi)
description: Deccan sultanate of the eastern plateau (Telangana and coastal Andhra), famed for its diamonds; annexed by Aurangzeb in 1687.

name: Gondwana (Gond kingdoms)
description: The Gond kingdoms of central India — Garha-Mandla, Deogarh, Chanda and Ratanpur — that ruled the forested Gondwana belt until the Marathas (Bhonsle) absorbed them in the mid-18th century.

name: Gwalior (Scindia)
description: A major Maratha-origin princely state of central India under the Scindias.
notableRulers: Scindia dynasty; founded by Ranoji Scindia

name: Hill Rajas (Himachal)
description: The patchwork of Himalayan Rajput hill states (Kangra/Katoch and others) before Sikh and then British control.

name: Holkar (Indore State)
description: A Maratha-origin princely state of Malwa under the Holkars.
notableRulers: Holkar dynasty; founded by Malhar Rao Holkar; regent Ahilyabai Holkar

name: Hoysala Kingdom
notableRulers: Rulers included: Ballala II, Ballala III, Narasimha I, Narasimha II, Narasimha III, Nripa Kama, Someshvara, Vinayaditya, Vishnuvardhana.

name: Hyderabad
description: The Nizam's dominions — the largest and richest princely state
notableRulers: Rose under Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I; fell under the last Nizam Osman Ali Khan (Operation Polo 1948)

name: Idu Mishmi
description: The Idu Mishmi of the Dibang valley, accomplished weavers and shamanic priests of the eastern Himalaya.

name: Ikkeri (Keladi) Nayak
description: Coastal-Karnataka kingdom of the Keladi Nayakas, absorbed by Hyder Ali of Mysore in 1763.

name: India
description: The Republic of India — independent from British rule in 1947 and a sovereign republic from 1950.
notableRulers: Rose under Jawaharlal Nehru as first PM

name: Jaintia Kingdom
description: Hill kingdom of the Jaintia (Pnar); annexed by the British in 1835.

name: Jaipur
description: The largest Rajputana state
notableRulers: Kachwaha dynasty; founded by Sawai Jai Singh II

name: Jaunpur Sultanate
notableRulers: Rulers included: Hussain Shah Sharqi, Ibrahim Shah Sharqi, Mahmud Shah, Malik Sarwar/Khwaja-i-Jahan, Mubarak Shah.

name: Jhalawar State
description: A Rajputana state carved out of Kota in 1838.

name: Jhansi
description: Maratha principality of Jhansi; lapsed in 1853; its Rani became an icon of the 1857 revolt.
notableRulers: Rulers included: Shiv Rao Bhau, Raghunath Rao Newalkar, Gangadhar Rao, Rani Lakshmibai.

name: Jind
description: A Sikh Phulkian state of the Punjab.

name: Jodhpur (Marwar)
description: The Rathore kingdom of Marwar in western Rajasthan.
notableRulers: Rulers included: Ajit Singh, Chandrasen, Hanwant Singh, Jaswant Singh, Maldeo, Man Singh, Rao Chunda, Rao Jodha, Rao Siha, Takht Singh, Umaid Singh.

name: Junagadh
description: A Kathiawar state whose ruler acceded to Pakistan in 1947; integrated into India after a plebiscite in 1948.

name: Kachari Kingdom
description: Dimasa-Kachari kingdom of the Barak valley; annexed by the British in 1832.

name: Kalachuri
notableRulers: Rulers included: Gangeyadeva, Gayakarna, Jayasimha, Karna, Kokalla I, Vamaraja, Vijayasimha, Yashahkarna.

name: Kalahandi State
description: A princely state of western Odisha.

name: Kalat (Khanate)
description: The largest Baloch state
notableRulers: Khanate of Kalat under the Ahmadzai khans

name: Kalhora (Sindh)
description: The Kalhora dynasty of Sindh, displaced by the Talpur Amirs in 1783.

name: Kapurthala
description: A Sikh princely state known for its Francophile architecture.

name: Karauli State
description: A Rajput state of eastern Rajputana claiming descent from Krishna.

name: Kathiawar Minor States
description: The dense patchwork of small Saurashtra (Kathiawar) princely states and estates.

name: Khairpur State
description: A Talpur-ruled princely state of Sindh.

name: Khampti
description: The Tai-Khampti, Theravada Buddhists who migrated from the Irrawaddy in the 18th century — the only Arunachal people with their own script — forming a chiefdom around Namsai.

name: Khasi States
description: Group of ~25 Khasi native states under British paramountcy, never directly ruled; acceded to India in 1947.

name: Kingdom of Coorg
description: Haleri kingdom of Coorg (Kodagu); annexed by the British in 1834.

name: Kolhapur
description: The senior Maratha principality of the Kolhapur Bhonsles (junior line of Shivaji's house); a princely state under British paramountcy from 1812 until 1949.

name: Kota
description: A Hadoti Rajput state carved out of Bundi.

name: Kumaon & Garhwal (local)
description: The Kumaon and Garhwal Himalayan kingdoms; overrun by Gorkha Nepal (1790s) and then annexed by the British in 1815.

name: Kutch
description: The large desert-and-coast kingdom of Kutch under the Jadejas.

name: Ladakh (Namgyal)
description: Buddhist kingdom of Ladakh under the Namgyal dynasty; conquered by the Dogras (Zorawar Singh) 1834-42.

name: Madurai Nayak
description: Telugu warrior-governors who became independent kings of the Tamil south after the decline of Vijayanagara.

name: Malwa Sultanate
notableRulers: Rulers included: Baz Bahadur, Dilawar Khan, Ghiyasuddin, Hoshang Shah, Mahmud II, Mahmud Khalji.

name: Mandi
description: A western-Himalayan hill state of the Beas valley.

name: Manipur
description: An ancient kingdom in the eastern hills; briefly fought the British in 1891

name: Maratha Empire
description: Confederacy of Maratha chiefs led by the Peshwa; the dominant power in 18th-century India before British paramountcy.

name: Mayurbhanj State
description: The largest Odisha princely state

name: Mishmi
description: The Digaru and Miju Mishmi of the Lohit and Anjaw hills, traders and weavers of the far eastern frontier.

name: Monpa & Sherdukpen
description: Mahayana-Buddhist Monpa and Sherdukpen peoples of the western Kameng hills, self-governed through village and clan councils.

name: Monpa (Tawang Monastery)
description: Tibetan-Buddhist Monpa people of the Tawang region, administered through the Tawang Monastery (founded 1681) under a parliamentary 'Kato' council linked to Lhasa, until India's integration in 1951.

name: Mughal Empire
description: The once-great empire, by the later 18th century reduced to titular authority around Delhi under Maratha then British protection.

name: Mysore
description: The Kingdom of Mysore under the Wadiyars — a model princely state in southern Karnataka.
notableRulers: Wadiyar dynasty; interrupted by Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan (1761–99); revived under the Crown

name: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
description: The Sultanat-i-Khudadad ('God-given state'). Hyder Ali seized power from the Wadiyars in 1761; his son Tipu Sultan, the Tiger of Mysore, ruled until he fell defending Seringapatam in 1799. A militarised, Persianate-Islamic state with its own flag, calendar, coinage and famous war-rockets, it fought four Anglo-Mysore Wars against the East India Company. After Tipu's death the British restored the Hindu Wadiyars as a princely state.

name: Nagpur (Bhonsle)
description: Bhonsle Maratha kingdom of Nagpur and Chhattisgarh; lapsed to the British in 1854.
notableRulers: Rulers included: Appa Sahib, Janoji, Mudhoji, Raghoji I, Raghoji II, Raghoji III.

name: Najib-ud-Daula (Rohilla)
description: Rohilla Afghan chief who, after the Third Battle of Panipat (1761), became regent (Mir Bakhshi) of the titular Mughal court and the effective ruler of Delhi until c.1771, when the Marathas under Mahadji Scindia retook the capital. The Mughal emperor remained on the throne in name throughout.

name: Nawanagar (Jamnagar)
description: A Kathiawar coastal state

name: Nepal
description: The Shah kingdom of Nepal — never colonised; effective power lay with the hereditary Rana prime ministers from 1846 to 1951.
notableRulers: United by Prithvi Narayan Shah; ruled in practice by Rana premiers

name: Nocte
description: The Nocte of the Patkai hills (Tirap), organised in powerful hereditary village chieftaincies.

name: Nyishi
description: The Nyishi, the largest people of Arunachal, living in clan-based village communities across the central hills.

name: Oiniwar
notableRulers: Rulers included: Bhogishvara, Ganeshvara, Kameshvara Thakur, Kirti Singh, Lakhima Devi regency, Shiva Singh, later Oiniwars.

name: Oman (Gwadar exclave)
description: The port of Gwadar — a coastal exclave of the Sultanate of Oman until sold to Pakistan in 1958.

name: Orchha
description: The senior Bundela Rajput state of Bundelkhand.

name: Orissa Princely States
description: The many feudatory states of Odisha (Mayurbhanj

name: Pakistan
description: The Islamic Republic of Pakistan — created at Partition in 1947 from the Muslim-majority north-west and east.

name: Pandya dynasty
notableRulers: Rulers included: Arikesari, Jatavarman Sundara, Kadungon, Maravarman Sundara, Varagunavarman, later Tenkasi Pandyas.

name: Panna
description: A Bundela state known for its diamond mines.

name: Paramara (Malwa)
notableRulers: Rulers included: Arjunavarman, Bhoja, Mahalakadeva, Munja/Vakpati II, Naravarman, Siyaka, Udayaditya, Upendra.

name: Pashtun tribal areas
description: Autonomous Pashtun tribal territory of the northwest frontier; never directly ruled, loosely under British influence after 1849.

name: Patiala
description: The premier Sikh princely state of the Punjab (a Phulkian state).
notableRulers: Phulkian (Sidhu) dynasty; founded by Ala Singh

name: Patna State (Balangir)
description: A western Odisha princely state (Patna State

name: Porbandar
description: A small Kathiawar port state — birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi.

name: Portuguese India
description: Portuguese coastal enclaves — Goa

name: Pudukkottai (Tondaiman)
description: The only princely state in the Tamil country
notableRulers: Rulers included: Martanda Bhairava, Raghunatha Raya Tondaiman, Rajagopala Tondaiman, Ramachandra Tondaiman, Vijaya Raghunatha.

name: Rajpipla
description: A forested princely state of eastern Gujarat.

name: Rajputana Minor States
description: Smaller Rajputana princely states beyond the major houses.

name: Ramnad (Setupati)
description: The Marava kingdom of Ramnad under the Sethupathis ('guardians of the bridge' to Rameswaram); a turbulent semi-independent power in the Tamil far south.

name: Rampur State
description: A Rohilla Pathan princely state of the upper Gangetic plain.

name: Rewa
description: The premier princely state of Baghelkhand in central India.

name: Rohilkhand (Rohillas)
description: Principality of Afghan (Rohilla) settlers in the upper Ganga plain; conquered by Awadh with British help in the Rohilla War of 1774.
notableRulers: Ali Mohammed Khan; Hafiz Rahmat Khan

name: Satara
description: The Maratha Chhatrapati's restored state of Satara; lapsed to the British in 1848.

name: Sawantwadi
description: Konkan coastal kingdom of the Sawant-Bhonsles; a princely state under the British until 1948.

name: Seraikela-Kharsawan
description: Two small adjoining princely states of the Chota Nagpur plateau.

name: Seuna (Yadava)
notableRulers: Rulers included: Bhillama V, Dridhaprahara, Harapaladeva, Jaitugi, Krishna, Mahadeva, Ramachandra, Shankaradeva, Singhana II.

name: Sikh Empire
description: Sikh Empire founded by Ranjit Singh; spanned Punjab, Kashmir and the northwest; annexed by the British in 1849.

name: Sikh misls
description: The Sikh confederacy of independent warbands that ruled the Punjab before Ranjit Singh unified them into the Sikh Empire (1799).

name: Sindh (Talpur Amirs)
description: Talpur Amirs of Sindh; conquered by Sir Charles Napier for the British in 1843.

name: Sirmaur
description: A Himalayan hill state of present-day Himachal Pradesh.

name: Sirohi State
description: A Rajput state at the foot of Mount Abu.

name: Mewar (Sisodia)
notableRulers: Rulers included: Amar Singh, Guhila/Bappa Rawal traditions, Kumbha, Pratap, Raj Singh, Rana Hammir, Sanga, Udai Singh II, later Maharanas to Bhupal Singh.

name: Sivaganga (Marava)
description: Marava chieftaincy that split from Ramnad; famed for early resistance to the British under the Maruthu brothers.

name: Sri Lanka
description: Independent Ceylon (1948)

name: Sur Empire
notableRulers: Rulers included: Firuz Shah, Ibrahim Suri, Islam Shah, Muhammad Adil Shah, Sher Shah Suri, Sikandar Suri.

name: Surguja State
description: A forested princely state of northern Chhattisgarh.

name: Tagin
description: The Tagin of the Upper Subansiri highlands.

name: Tangsa
description: The Tangsa (and Singpho) peoples of the Patkai foothills around Changlang.

name: Tanjore (Thanjavur) Nayak
description: Nayak kingdom of the Kaveri delta; a centre of Tamil and Telugu culture, later taken by the Marathas of Tanjore.

name: Tehri Garhwal State
description: The Garhwal kingdom of the Himalayas

name: Thanjavur (Maratha)
description: The Maratha kingdom of Thanjavur, founded by Shivaji's half-brother Venkoji (Ekoji); a great patron of Tamil and Carnatic culture, it became a British protectorate in 1799 and was annexed in 1856.

name: Tomara dynasty of Gwalior
notableRulers: Rulers included: Dungarendra Singh, Kalyanmal, Kirti Singh, Man Singh Tomar, Vikramaditya, Vir Singh Dev.

name: Tonk
description: Muslim-ruled princely state in Rajputana, founded by the Pindari leader Amir Khan.

name: Travancore
description: A prosperous princely state of the Kerala coast

name: Tripura
description: A long-lived hill kingdom of the north-east under the Manikya kings.
notableRulers: Rulers included: Bir Bikram Kishore, Bir Chandra, Dhanya Manikya, Govinda Manikya, Krishna Manikya, Ratna Manikya, Vijaya Manikya II.

name: Udaipur (Mewar)
description: The senior-most Rajput house — Mewar under the Sisodias
notableRulers: Sisodia dynasty of Mewar; Maharana Pratap

name: Vijayanagara Empire
capital: Hampi (Vijayanagara) to 1565; then Penukonda, Chandragiri (1592) & Vellore (1604)

name: Wancho
description: The Wancho of the Longding hills, known for their wood-carving and strong chiefly village democracies.

name: Kadathanadu
description: A kingdom of North Malabar ruled by the Porlathiri dynasty (dispossessed rulers of Polanad), centred near Vatakara. Its coast is where the French established Mahé in 1725; absorbed by Mysore in Hyder Ali's 1766 conquest of Malabar.

name: Central Kerala principalities
description: The independent Nair kingdoms of central Kerala between Cochin and Venad — Thekkumkur, Vadakkumkur, Kayamkulam, Ambalapuzha (Chembakassery) and Purakkad. They were annexed by Marthanda Varma's Travancore between 1742 and 1753.

name: Mukunda Deva
description: The last independent Hindu king of Odisha (of the Bhoi–Chalukya line). He overthrew the Bhoi rulers in 1560 and ruled until the Karrani Sultans of Bengal conquered Odisha in 1568.

name: Kingdom of Sikkim (Namgyal)
description: The Himalayan kingdom of Sikkim, ruled by the Namgyal dynasty of Chogyals from 1642. A British protectorate from 1861 and an Indian protectorate from 1950, it remained a monarchy until it merged with India in 1975.
notableRulers: Rulers included: Chakdor, Gyurmed, Palden Thondup Namgyal, Phuntsog Namgyal, Sidkeong, Tashi, Tensung, Tenzing, Tsugphud.

name: Kampili Kingdom
capital: Kampili / Kummata (Anegundi), on the Tungabhadra near Hampi

name: Chutia (Sadiya) Kingdom
notableRulers: Rulers included: Birpal, Dharmanarayan, Gauradhwajpal, Jayadhwajpal, Karmadhwajpal, Laksminarayan, Mayuradhwajpal, Nitypal, Ratnadhwajpal, Sankhadhwajpal, Satyanarayan, Vijayadhwajpal, Vikramadhwajpal.

name: Khurda (Bhoi)
description: Hindu kingdom of Khurda (Bhoi dynasty), guardians of the Jagannath temple at Puri, 1568–1804.
notableRulers: Ramachandra Deva I; Purushottama Deva; Divyasingha Deva

name: Udaiyarpalayam
description: A Tamil palayam (poligar chiefdom) in the Ariyalur country, founded by Chinna Nalla Kalatkal Tola Udaiyar and shielded by dense forest and broken terrain. It kept its own court at Udaiyarpalayam, a lion flag and a Varaha ensign, and struck its own coin, the Udaiyarpalayam pudhupanam, ruling as a quasi-independent vassal under Vijayanagara, the Gingee Nayaks and later the Nawab of Arcot, who annexed it in January 1765; the family continued as zamindars until 1956.
notableRulers: Chinna Nalla Kalatkal Tola Udaiyar (founder); the Udaiyar poligars
